headline: Record quarter with margin expansion, guidance holds pace
summary_short: Arista's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 37.7% y/y (+12.1% q/q) to $3,035.7M, its first quarter above $3 billion, with GAAP operating margin expanding to 45.4% and diluted EPS up 35.7% y/y to $0.95.
summary_long: Revenue grew 37.7% y/y and 12.1% q/q to $3,035.7M on broad-based product and service demand, crossing $3 billion for the first time. GAAP operating margin expanded to 45.4% (non-GAAP 49.9%) and gross margin held at 62.9%, up q/q but down 2.3ppt y/y on mix. Diluted EPS rose to $0.95 GAAP ($1.02 non-GAAP), up 35.7% y/y. Cash and equivalents fell 17.9% q/q to $2,290.2M as the company shifted funds into marketable securities (up to $11,053.1M), while stockholders' equity grew to $14,797.7M. No shares were repurchased in H1 2026, versus $983.0M in H1 2025. For Q3 2026, Arista guided revenue to approximately $3.3B, non-GAAP operating margin to 48-49%, and non-GAAP diluted EPS to $1.06-$1.08.

drivers.explanation: CFO attributed the quarter to "strong, broad-based growth", and CEO cited the 'Arista 2.0' platform strategy across AI, data center, and campus; no further segment-level breakdown is disclosed.
Product revenue rose to $2,605.2M from $1,877.0M y/y and service revenue to $430.5M from $327.8M y/y; the release does not attribute the acceleration to a specific product line or customer segment.
y/y margin compression to 62.9% from 65.2% is disclosed only via the reconciliation tables; the release gives no narrative cause (e.g. mix shift) for the decline.

Operating expenses grew slower than revenue (total opex +17.7% y/y vs revenue +37.7% y/y), expanding GAAP operating margin to 45.4% from 44.7%; this is arithmetic operating leverage, not separately explained in the release.
Cash fell q/q because the company shifted funds into marketable securities (purchases of $4,328.9M in the six-month cash flow statement) rather than a change in operating performance.
